units.name: KH-DR-01
units.text: | KH-DR-01 | Renaming or moving a representation preserves semantic identity; a different concept receives a different identity. | Definition Modelling; §§3, 5.1. |

units.name: KH-DR-02
units.text: | KH-DR-02 | Committed revisions, source captures and relationship histories remain immutable and inspectable. | Definition Modelling / Evidence; §§5, 21.4. |

units.name: KH-DR-03
units.text: | KH-DR-03 | Every committed assertion satisfies its pinned type, direction, endpoint and multiplicity constraints. | Definition Modelling; §§8, 17. |

units.name: KH-DR-04
units.text: | KH-DR-04 | Every complete baseline resolves explicit compatible versions, including its ontology/profile and required artifacts. | Definition Modelling; §§5.1, 16–17. |

units.name: KH-DR-05
units.text: | KH-DR-05 | Sources and interpretations identify exact revisions and anchors; refreshing a source preserves previous citations. | Evidence and Provenance; §5.2. |

units.name: KH-DR-06
units.text: | KH-DR-06 | Each normative field or relationship has one declared owner; document and graph updates preserve that ownership coherently. | Definition Modelling; §§3, 5.2, 21.5. |

units.name: KH-DR-07
units.text: | KH-DR-07 | Read, commit, review and operation-result access use current scoped host authority; modelled roles confer no runtime privilege. | Governance; §§13, 21.3–21.4. |

units.name: KH-DR-08
units.text: | KH-DR-08 | One model-branch change set commits all definitions, documents, provenance, history, head and recovery receipt together, or leaves the accepted head unchanged. | Governance with storage port; §§21.4–21.6. |

units.name: KH-DR-09
units.text: | KH-DR-09 | Expected-head and relevant revision/graph guards hold at publication; stale work cannot silently replace current work. | Governance / Definition Modelling; §§21.4, 21.7. |

units.name: KH-DR-10
units.text: | KH-DR-10 | After current authority checks, an exact retry resolves the original result; operation identity reused for different intent is rejected. | Governance; §21.4. |

units.name: KH-DR-11
units.text: | KH-DR-11 | Acknowledged success survives recovery in the tested durability profile; an uncertain caller can inspect the original operation outcome without a new mutation. | Governance / file adapter; §21.6. |

units.name: KH-DR-12
units.text: | KH-DR-12 | A read resolves one snapshot; derived views disclose their snapshot or watermark and cannot override authoritative resolution. | Definition Modelling / query use cases; §21.7. |

units.name: KH-DR-13
units.text: | KH-DR-13 | A review binds exact scope/revisions. Storage commitment, review approval, implementation, verification and human acceptance remain separate facts. | Governance; §§14, 17. |

units.name: KH-DR-14
units.text: | KH-DR-14 | Import validates staged content and source/endpoint resolution before promotion; export preserves the selected profile's declared semantics and recovery history. | Interchange; §§16, 21.9. |

units.name: KH-DR-15
units.text: | KH-DR-15 | The consumer API preserves model meaning across storage choices and does not expose native storage transactions or layout. | Application boundary; §§21.2–21.3, 21.7–21.9. |

units.name: KH-DR-16
units.text: | KH-DR-16 | The user's full-ontology target requires explicit versioned definitions/schemas and meaningful conformance for every source catalogue type/relationship and specialised contract; a seed or label list cannot establish full support. | Definition Modelling; §§5–17; clarified user scope, 31 October 2026. |

units.name: KH-DR-17
units.text: | KH-DR-17 | Native kernel subjects and successor revisions share exact typed addressing and immutable lineage; selected baselines resolve their actual subjects without shadow definitions, circular hash assumptions or latest substitution. | Definition Modelling / Evidence / Governance; §§4–5, 8, 21.4. |

units.name: KH-DR-18
units.text: | KH-DR-18 | Available vocabulary, valid structure, purpose completeness, applicability, observed execution and human assessment are separate facts. Draft gaps cannot waive integrity and inapplicable self-model families remain supported ontology vocabulary. | Definition Modelling / Evidence; §§3–4, 6, 14, 17. |

units.name: KH-DR-19
units.text: | KH-DR-19 | Typed navigation is finite, ordered and bound to exact selection/intent; continuations recheck current disclosure and cannot mix later head revisions or another actor's scope. | Definition Modelling / Governance; §§21.3/21.7. |

units.name: Hub
units.text: | Hub | Governed repository containing model scopes and policy references. | Neither a production transaction store nor a source-code repository. |

units.name: System model
units.text: | System model | Coherent definition of a particular system with scope and owner. | The KnowledgeHub library is one system that can be described. |

units.name: Ontology / profile
units.text: | Ontology / profile | Versioned vocabulary, permitted relationships, constraints and selected completeness obligations. | Type availability differs from completeness for a purpose. |

units.name: Ontology conformance
units.text: | Ontology conformance | A record/graph conforms to its exact registered property, endpoint and constraint definitions. | A familiar type name or arbitrary property bag does not establish support. |

units.name: Kernel subject
units.text: | Kernel subject | An addressable native identity, exact revision, assertion, anchor or representation binding. | A relationship targeting an assertion or revision must not require a duplicate editable element. |

units.name: Model completeness
units.text: | Model completeness | Applicable obligations are met for a declared purpose and exact selection, with explicit draft gaps/inapplicability. | A complete self-model does not prove support for unused ontology families or human acceptance. |

units.name: Element identity
units.text: | Element identity | Stable semantic identity within a declared namespace and scope. | A filename, label or position is not its identity. |

units.name: Element revision
units.text: | Element revision | Immutable definition of that identity at a particular version. | Editing creates a successor; it does not rewrite cited history. |

units.name: Relationship assertion
units.text: | Relationship assertion | Identified, versioned claim of a typed relation between exact endpoints. | A drawn arrow or similar label does not establish the relation. |

units.name: Source artifact / revision / anchor
units.text: | Source artifact / revision / anchor | Source identity, exact captured bytes or immutable version, and a meaningful location within it. | Refreshing a source does not refresh previous citations. |

units.name: Interpretation
units.text: | Interpretation | Account of how a source supports a definition or assertion, with author and review status. | Extracted content and confidence are distinct from approval. |

units.name: Definition authority
units.text: | Definition authority | Declared representation that owns a field or relationship in a scope. | This is different from the caller's permission to change it. |

units.name: Snapshot / commit
units.text: | Snapshot / commit | Consistent immutable stored generation and the accepted change that produced it. | Storage commitment does not mean the design was approved. |

units.name: Model branch / head
units.text: | Model branch / head | Scope whose current committed snapshot can advance under guards. | A head selects a state; it is not an ontology revision. |

units.name: Model baseline
units.text: | Model baseline | Explicit selection of compatible element, relationship, ontology and artifact revisions. | A named baseline is not an implicit query for latest. |

units.name: Change set
units.text: | Change set | One requested, atomic change to one model branch, with base, operation identity and intent. | A project OpenSpec change can require many runtime change sets. |

units.name: Review decision
units.text: | Review decision | Assessment of an exact scope and revisions by an authorised reviewer. | Approval of a definition is neither implementation nor verification. |

units.name: Implementation evidence
units.text: | Implementation evidence | Versioned artifact or observed result tied to the claim it supports. | A specification or a successful import does not establish that claim. |

units.name: Delivery slice
units.text: | Delivery slice | Demonstrable increment with actor, outcome, complete path, safeguards and evidence. | Adopted project delivery convention from the manual, not a formal DDD construct. |

units.name: KH-D-01
units.text: | KH-D-01 | Adopted: versioned kernel + `Requirement`, `UseCase` and `satisfies`; fixed seed contract below. | Implement and verify only this profile first; reject arbitrary types/properties. |

units.name: KH-D-02
units.text: | KH-D-02 | Adopted: Markdown owns narrative; graph owns semantic IDs, types and assertions; coherent API submission owns admission. | Bind fields/fragments exactly; later authoring round-trip remains KH-SL-002. |

units.name: KH-D-03
units.text: | KH-D-03 | Adopted: Rust 2024, fixed Rust 1.85 minimum, host-owned Tokio 1.x for the file backend; bounded blocking jobs. | User's later directive selects existing Rust 1.99.1, no compiler installation and assumed platform compliance. Record actual runs separately; no minimum-compiler execution claim. |

units.name: KH-D-04
units.text: | KH-D-04 | Adopted: Linux x86_64/local ext4, coordinated single-host writers, immutable generations and synced atomic reference publication. | First evidence covers process interruption and lost responses; power-loss and other filesystem/host support await separate evidence. |

units.name: KH-D-05
units.text: | KH-D-05 | Adopted: trusted host supplies stable actor identity and current scoped policy; deny by default. | No built-in account system or privilege from modelled roles; no mandatory human-review workflow in the seed. |

units.name: KH-D-06
units.text: | KH-D-06 | Adopted: separate explicit versions, SHA-256, RFC 8785 canonical request encoding, branch-scoped operation IDs and lifetime committed-receipt retention. | Implement compatibility, replay and integrity checks under the contract below; no pruning in the first slice. |

units.name: KH-D-07
units.text: | KH-D-07 | Direction retained: bounded portable snapshot queries. KH-D-14 proposes the exact-type/ID and directional subset needed next; broader operators remain open. | Initial seed has exact-ID reads only. Review the proposed finite ordering/cursor contract before implementing the new subset. |

units.name: KH-D-08
units.text: | KH-D-08 | Direction retained: host-configured review of exact revisions, separate from commitment and evidence. Detailed roles, outcomes and dispute policy remain open. | Resolve before KH-SL-004. |

units.name: KH-D-09
units.text: | KH-D-09 | Direction retained: distinct model-exchange and recovery-backup profiles. Collision mapping and replay-domain continuity remain open. | Resolve before KH-SL-005; ordinary exchange cannot silently promise recovery continuity. |

units.name: KH-D-10
units.text: | KH-D-10 | Direction retained: progressive self-description with an explicit scoped handover. The next change proposes a full applicable self-model; exact acceptance/handover baseline remains open. | KH-SL-008 proposes the model, while KH-SL-006 still owns actual authority transfer. Documents retain authority until that decision. |

units.name: KH-D-11
units.text: | KH-D-11 | `system-definition-ontology/1`, explicit shared typed schemas and per-type refinements covering 17 kernel kinds, 128 profile kinds, all 32 catalogue signatures plus separately sourced/refined prose edges; `knowledgehub-self-description/1` selects applicable completeness. | The coverage inventory defines every row; source omissions and chosen field requiredness remain visibly proposed refinements. No family may be silently omitted to declare completion. |

units.name: KH-D-12
units.text: | KH-D-12 | Small trusted meta-schema, first-class exact ontology/kernel addressing, closed deterministic validators and independent binary/original source capture with resolving locator manifests. | One owner per subject/property; no shadow assertion/revision nodes, arbitrary script execution or inferred PDF/Markdown equivalence. Host-derived extraction observations remain distinct from review. |

units.name: KH-D-13
units.text: | KH-D-13 | Append-only successors plus selected normative revision maps and immutable exact named baseline closure; explicit relationship pins and deterministic comparison. | Preserve original explanations and review scope; no automatic latest lookup, rebase or repinning. Historical supporting artifact revisions are not competing normative owners. |

units.name: KH-D-14
units.text: | KH-D-14 | Exact type/ID filters, qualified forward/reverse traversal and stable UTF-8-ID ordering; default/max depth 1/4, page 100/1000, total visited subject/edge caps 10000 each. Opaque actor/query-bound instance cursors: 64 active, explicit release, 30-minute idle expiry, invalid after close/reopen. | Concrete next subset of KH-D-07. Current policy applies to every page; limits and invalid-cursor outcomes are public. Broader operators and durable cursors are not promised. |

units.name: KH-D-15
units.text: | KH-D-15 | Explicit opt-in files/request/record version 2; preallocated opaque revision tokens separate from canonical content digests, enabling cyclic exact references. Keep original version-1 codecs, seed semantics, hashes and receipts exact. | Full catalogue/self-model use fresh v2 stores. No silent in-place migration, circular hash scheme or transfer of old committed keys to a new replay domain. |
